ranking.reader: Artem, a full-stack engineer who builds web products and LLM agents and writes about both. He wants items he can learn from or act on as a builder, not general tech news.

topics.description: Agent and automated pipelines and harnesses, LLM assistants, self-hosted/private AI platform development, and LLM/inference optimization.
exclude: AI policy, lawsuits, regulation, company drama, funding and business news
coding agents and their add-ons (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, plugins, skills) used while writing code (they belong to Tooling)
consumer AI apps with no engineering substance
include: building, running or evaluating LLM systems: agent harnesses, tool use, MCP, RAG, evals
inference and serving: self-hosted/local models, quantization, speed and cost
major model, API or dev-platform releases that change what or how you build
topics.name: AI Engineering

topics.description: Tools developers use to build software: editors, CLIs, libraries, and AI coding tools.
exclude: components for building LLM systems: agent frameworks, inference servers, evals (they belong to AI Engineering)
games, consumer apps, and utilities with no role in software development
nostalgia or legacy-systems threads, career and workplace discussion
include: tools used while building software: editors and IDEs, CLIs, terminals, debuggers, build tools, package managers, version control, databases
AI tools used while writing code: coding agents, editor plugins, Claude Code skills and hooks
new or notably improved open-source libraries and frameworks for building software
topics.name: Tooling

topics.description: Product and web trends, securities & market data, data visualization, browser performance, web architecture, and SEO.
exclude: general tech-company news, earnings and stock moves with no product angle
AI model releases (AI Engineering) and developer tools (Tooling)
games and demos that merely run in a browser
include: the web platform and browsers: new APIs, standards, rendering and browser performance
frontend engineering and web architecture: frameworks, CSS, performance, SEO
data visualization, and products built on market or financial data
product and web trends: notable launches and how web products make money
topics.name: Web Products

items.summary: Google plans to support a shared AI training control in robots.txt: a single 'policy token' letting sites opt out across participating AI providers, based on IETF AIPREF work and running alongside Google-Extended.
items.title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites

items.summary: InferSSD is an Apache-2.0 project built on llama.cpp that runs large mixture-of-experts GGUF models from SSD when they exceed RAM/VRAM, with browser chat and an OpenAI-compatible API. Its benchmarks claim up to 4.85× prefill and 3.29× decode speedups over llama.cpp on the same hardware.
items.title: wici-ai/inferssd

items.summary: DSH-Android runs the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) agent natively on an Android phone without root or Termux: Node 24 is compiled into the app and driven via dsh's SDK protocol, with Kotlin device tools for screen reading, taps and system settings, optional Shizuku, and scheduling triggers.
items.title: jackwener/DSH-Android

items.summary: A Chinese-language self-study course for Python developers on building AI agents, based on Stanford CS329Z public materials: 19 lessons plus 4 hands-on exercises covering LLMs, RAG, tool calling, memory, multi-agent collaboration and safety, shipped as Markdown sources with an offline HTML reader.
items.title: wanghao-SunSky/cs329z-chinese

items.summary: Mika is an Apache-2.0 Android agent app (public beta) that executes one-sentence requests on a private background screen while you keep using the phone, with a built-in browser and local Linux sandbox. An adb-forwarded MCP endpoint lets desktop AI tools dispatch tasks to it; you supply your own model API key.
items.title: wangzan101/Mika

items.summary: hnoss, an immediate-mode TUI library for Odin, written in pure Odin with no C or ncurses bindings, shipping widgets, braille graphs, truecolor 60 fps double-buffered diffing and layout tools. Installable only as a git submodule or clone since Odin has no package manager.
items.title: Huseynteymurzade28/hnoss

items.summary: Lasm, a toolchain that compiles ordinary Lean 4 programs ahead of time to WebAssembly, so one codebase can target Node, serverless/edge functions, WASI or the browser with proved properties; it ships on npm and bundles Lean 4.35.0, needing only Node/Bun/Deno.
items.title: Show HN: Lasm – Write formally verified webapps in Lean for Node/serverless/edge

items.summary: Phorion's write-up on a backdoored official Claude Code for VS Code extension bundle on the Cursor Marketplace (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) that drops a persistent SSH backdoor on macOS, Linux and Windows. Cursor has removed the affected versions.
items.title: Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace

items.summary: Pico CSS, a minimal CSS framework for semantic HTML, has ended maintenance: v2.1.1 is the final release and repositories are archived, while npm, jsDelivr, and the site remain online. The author cites AI-generated lightweight HTML and says a modern-CSS rewrite would be a different project.
items.title: Pico CSS is no longer maintained

items.summary: ElementaryUI lets builders run declarative Swift applications natively in the browser via WebAssembly, using SwiftUI-like @View and @State syntax for UI and event handling.
items.title: ElementaryUI – Swift, in the Browser

items.summary: Ahrefs' September 2026 product update roundup covers five changes, including a new Site Audit AI Discoverability issue category, an Organic pages by type widget in Site Explorer, and semantic filters in Keywords Explorer.
items.title: AI Discoverability, Page types, and more (September 2026)

items.summary: NamiAgent is a Chinese-language tutorial and runnable local AI agent that builds an agent from a minimal while loop through tools, permissions, context, skills, MCP, subagents, planning and memory, with a web UI and per-lesson code snapshots.
items.title: aa1143/NamiAgent

items.summary: graphmemory is a bitemporal memory service for AI agents with valid-time and record-time axes, six-variable decay, TTL expiry, deduplication and competitive retrieval, built on Graphiti, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Redis, and exposed via MCP tools and a web GUI.
items.title: gh9ko8y/graphmemory

items.summary: sapper-v2 is a legion-style multi-agent AI system for authorized penetration testing that won the 3rd Tencent Cloud Intelligent Attack-Defense Challenge qualifier, using a commander, parallel generals/soldiers and a layered fact graph, framed by the Nüwa Test.
items.title: N1nEmAn/sapper-v2

items.summary: persona-ai-sdk is a TypeScript SDK for AI characters that combines a persona catalog with a provider-neutral memory and response runtime, separating personas, memory, model, persistence and interface, and published on npm.
items.title: tavern-labs-ai/persona-ai-sdk

items.summary: GitHub repo for pursr, a Node.js package bundling browser visual QA: one CLI for capture, diff, sweep and audit, an MCP stdio server built on the official SDK with persistent tabs and actions, and a library API with 25 subpath modules. The page also fronts an admin-rights, password-protected loader.
items.title: Venomsphinx/pursr-rpocket

items.summary: Ghostman, a keyboard-driven terminal API client and webhook inspector pitched as a local-first Postman alternative: ~30MB RAM, ~150ms cold boot, collections saved as plain JSON/YAML in ~/.ghostman/, and a built-in webhook listener on port 9090.
items.title: Show HN: Ghostman – A fast, keyboard-driven TUI API client and webhook inspector

items.summary: A Bun --preload script (no-agent-summary.js) that stops Claude Code from re-sending each background agent's full transcript to its model roughly every 30 seconds just to fill status lines, without modifying the binary; the author's telemetry put agent_summary at 16.4% of spend.
items.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent’s transcript to its model

items.summary: A benchmark of the AI cost of JavaScript frameworks has agents build a small Pokémon app with frameworks such as Next.js, Nuxt, and SvelteKit, then tests outputs against a spec conformance suite and evaluates development time, tokens spent, and lines.
items.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks

items.summary: An MIT Press Reader article arguing, via a 1580 map, that data visualization is never neutral.
items.title: A 1580 Map Shows Why Data Visualization Is Never Neutral

items.summary: Charts of median graduate income by college and major, based on Department of Education data and an HEA Group analysis, show how school and major affect earnings. The article includes a searchable college-and-major comparison and links to downloadable data.
items.title: Cost of college versus the return on investement

items.summary: A harness for running LLM agents that play Minecraft via Mineflayer, with pluggable models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible endpoints), restart-surviving sessions, per-agent sandboxed shells, JSON-defined teams, and experimental vision. It ships a dev Paper server and was tested with 50 agents and Bed Wars matches.
items.title: yc-software/minecraft-agent-harness

items.summary: AnyModelBot is a local-first, MIT-licensed AI agent app for Windows, macOS and Linux, where each bot has its own persona, default model, workspace and memory, reachable via WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, Slack and Discord. All models come through Modelflare, billed per token with routing across 70+ models and cache-hit compensation.
items.title: modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot

items.summary: A real-time vision plugin for DSH that captures your screen, camera or video, scores each frame's change (0-255 HSV diff on a 64x36 grid) and only sends frames that changed, tiling 4-8 of them into one image to cut token cost. Published on npm, installed via dsh plugin, Apache-2.0 licensed.
items.title: SAOS-3624/dsh-see-now

items.summary: A post announcing LongCat-2.5, described in the title as offering native multimodality for agentic tasks.
items.title: LongCat-2.5: Native Multimodality for Agentic Tasks

items.summary: OmniDiff is an open-source content-aware Git difftool written in Rust that selects diff algorithms by file type and claims sub-100ms speed, robust coverage, and high accuracy across code, images, fonts, archives, PDFs, and message catalogs; prebuilt binaries and package installs are provided.
items.title: Show HN: OmniDiff – Opensource, super fast, content aware Git difftool, in Rust

items.summary: Uncut is a lossless, headless coding-agent harness: one 7 MB static Go binary, four tools, plain stdin/stdout, no TUI or telemetry. It sends the full conversation every model call, never truncates context, and exits on provider output cuts instead of returning partial answers.
items.title: Balanov/uncut

items.summary: Pi-Remote is a companion tool for the pi terminal coding agent that uses pi’s official extension API to mirror a live local session in the browser and allow remote messages and commands, including model/thinking changes and session navigation, across multiple devices.
items.title: Xpropel/Pi-Remote

items.summary: Explainer of the headingoffset HTML attribute, which adjusts heading levels by adding an offset and cascades through nested elements. Notes Firefox Nightly 153 shipped it behind a flag, so cross-browser support is still needed before use.
items.title: Overriding Heading Levels With the headingoffset HTML Attribute

items.summary: Stripe case study on moving its own vendor payments to Global Payouts. It says over $1B went to 3,400+ vendors by October 2026, new-market setup dropped from six weeks to one, and payouts held a 99.9% success rate.
items.title: Stripe on Stripe: What we learned moving $1B in vendor payments to Global Payouts

items.summary: A 20-year retrospective on Zamzar, a bootstrapped file-conversion SaaS run by two brothers, recounting milestones such as 766M files converted, 2,128 conversion types, and over 1M API requests per day.
items.title: Running a bootstrapped SaaS for 20 years with my brother

items.summary: Blog post reporting that GPT-6 Astra can natively read and write neural network weights, a capability the authors call Weight-Space Programming. Without gradient training it edited 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights, lifting MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and tripling IFEval.
items.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen

items.summary: Skein, an open-source execution control plane for local agent swarms that runs explicit task graphs with bounded concurrency and a persistent epoch fence, so an emergency stop invalidates queued work and rejects late completions. Version 0.2.0 is an early release installed as a static Go binary.
items.title: Balanov/skein

items.summary: Ask HN thread asking what hardware people use to run local LLMs day to day, with 42 comments sharing setups such as a single RTX 5090, clustered ASUS GX10 systems running DeepSeek, and Qwen models around 30B.
items.title: Ask HN: What hardware are you using to run local LLMs?

items.summary: Interactive notes covering RLHF, attention, LoRA, and LLM evals.
items.title: Show HN: Interactive notes on RLHF, attention, LoRA and LLM evals

items.summary: OpenAI's post on Pando, a new horizontally scalable backend for its monorepo's Git repositories that keeps Git protocol and client compatibility. It cut median push latency nearly 5x and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data daily.
items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI

items.summary: readme-visual-kit, a local SVG renderer plus portable Agent Skill that turns source-cited project descriptions into three README diagrams (flow, architecture, quickstart) with no API key or third-party runtime dependencies. v0.1.0 is an offline MVP.
items.title: tianfuzhibuyuci/readme-visual-kit

items.summary: Firezone introduces sanstun, a sans-IO Rust implementation of the WireGuard state machine with a parallel-friendly, idiomatic API aimed at ease of use, security and performance. It recounts moving off a heavily patched boringtun fork.
items.title: Sanstun: A sans-IO, parallel-friendly WireGuard implementation in Rust

items.summary: A Smashing Magazine article argues modern CSS can trade local simplicity for system complexity: smaller diffs may introduce bugs through interactions with JavaScript, layout, the cascade, and rendering, and it examines debugging split CSS/JS logic.
items.title: Modern CSS Might Make Your Front-End More Complex

items.summary: A FlowingData item highlights Christine Zhang’s New York Times piece on election-night “mirages,” explaining why percentage shifts can seem to favor a candidate artificially without context.
items.title: Election night mirages

items.summary: Safari 27.3 beta adds Adaptive Dark Mode, which automatically converts light websites to dark when enabled by a user, using a color matrix that preserves hue and targets WCAG 4.5:1 contrast; sites signaling color-scheme support are left unchanged.
items.title: Safari introduces Adaptive Dark Mode in 27.3

items.summary: A blog post testing an example from the “Sparks of Weight-Space Programming” paper reports that Qwen 3.8 27B running on a laptop can interpret raw model weights, extending the paper’s weight-reading and weight-editing claims beyond frontier models.
items.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too

items.summary: A hands-on article on dual-booting Linux on the Nvidia RTX Spark laptop finds GPU clocks locked near 780 MHz because of Windows-only encrypted power firmware, cutting GPT-OSS-120B inference from 65.4 to 13.9 tokens/s; WSL avoids the issue.
items.title: Nvidia RTX Spark encrypted firmware slows inference speed to 35% on Linux

items.summary: A GitHub repository curating 309 self-hostable open-source AI projects across local LLMs, agents, MCP servers, RAG, speech and image generation; a weekly GitHub API check moves archived, deleted or year-silent projects to an unmaintained list.
items.title: glincker/awesome-selfhosted-ai

items.summary: A README for EXZA Remote, a proprietary hosted MCP service that connects ChatGPT, Claude and other AI assistants to a user’s Mac, Windows or Linux computer for owner-approved file inspection, process checks and terminal commands, with warnings against an unofficial npx install.
items.title: exzade/EXZA-Remote

items.summary: Agent Autoloop is a lightweight automation kernel for command-line agents that schedules tasks, routes work to pluggable agents, and sends approval cards via Feishu, Slack, Discord or desktop notifications only when needed; runs locally on macOS/Linux.
items.title: KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop

items.summary: Code-review-skill is an evidence-backed, static-first code review skill for Claude Code and Codex, with English/Chinese packages, JSON-derived delivery summaries, auditable findings with locations, contracts and severity, plus gate decisions; no build or test run required.
items.title: kyy-logs/code-review-skill

items.summary: Codemap generates one HTML page mapping a Go module: packages, internal dependencies, and functions per file, with search, package usage views, and GitHub line jumps; it runs via go run or a GitHub Action, and tests are omitted.
items.title: Show HN: Codemap – one-page interactive map of any Go repository

items.summary: An Ahrefs analysis of OpenAI publisher licensing deals and ChatGPT citations finds partner domains' share of top citations rose from 7.5% in March 2026 to 15.8% in July and 12.5% in late September; ten partners rank among ChatGPT's 50 most-cited sites.
items.title: Every OpenAI Publisher Partnership, and How Often ChatGPT Cites Them

items.summary: An Ahrefs study of 10,000 brands and 260M non-branded AI prompts finds Reddit mentions correlate most strongly with AI visibility (~0.75), while press coverage (0.67) trails general webpage mentions (0.70); ChatGPT is least tied to off-site mentions.
items.title: Which Types of Mentions Correlate the Strongest With AI Visibility? (260M AI Prompts Analyzed)

items.summary: Release notes for Safari Technology Preview 256, a WebKit build for macOS Golden Gate and macOS Tahoe, list fixes and new CSS support including text-combine-upright on ::marker, continue: collapse with line-clamp, and font-palette-mix() on Cocoa.
items.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 256

items.summary: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview: a dense open-weight model pretrained on 12T tokens with 1M context, claiming U.S. open-weight SOTA on TerminalBench 2.1 (80.52) and trained for $32M — about one-tenth the prior cost — and served via Hugging Face, Together, OpenRouter and others.
items.title: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding

items.summary: Post laying out three architecture patterns for multi-agent systems — orchestrator-worker, blackboard, and pipeline — plus the coordination failure modes that surface only after a single-agent demo goes into unattended production.
items.title: Building a Multi-Agent System from Scratch: Architecture Patterns

items.summary: Post on the MCP OAuth redirect-URI allowlist dilemma: servers either reject self-hosted clients or, per a 2026 study of 119 servers, accept arbitrary redirect URIs and open a one-click phishing hole into users' storage.
items.title: Letting users trust their own MCP clients, without opening a phishing hole

items.summary: Rivet, a YC W23 actor-model orchestrator for agentic workloads: 72 KB per actor, 4.99 ms p99 cold starts, per-actor SQLite on S3 at SSD-like latency, idle hibernation, and a rivetkit TypeScript example.
items.title: Launch HN: Rivet (YC W23) – Scale and Orchestrate Agents on S3

items.summary: Gauge, an open-source CLI for "hillclimbing Agent Experience": it runs real coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode) against your docs, Skills, CLIs, SDKs or MCPs, captures where they get stuck, and lets your agent validate fixes locally via Docker before release.
items.title: Show HN: Gauge – Open-Source CLI to recursively improve your docs

items.summary: Browser-based SQLite editor that opens .sqlite/.db files, .sql dumps or CSV, lets you edit in a grid or with SQL, then exports a freshly rebuilt file; nothing is uploaded, and files are rebuilt on save rather than edited in place.
items.title: Edit an SQLite database in your browser

items.summary: Zero-dependency CLI that decodes Uniswap v4 revert data, unwrapping WrappedError from PoolManager and Universal Router's ExecutionFailed to show the hook selector, reason and errors; supports custom error signatures via --sig.
items.title: zhouxingchi1017/v4revert

items.summary: Stripe now lets compatible AI agents like Claude and Cursor access users' Stripe analytics data via its MCP or the Queries and Reports APIs, so natural-language prompts can build dashboards or decks. The Queries API is free through Jan 31, 2027, then credit-based.
items.title: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent

items.summary: FlowingData post on a Bloomberg map that uses mountain peaks—taller for bigger shifts, blue and red for party—to show movement toward Democrats and Republicans, which the author prefers to the NYT's arrow-based map for spotting the few Republican shifts.
items.title: Mountain peaks to show the shifts

items.summary: A Wall Street Journal election map combines county-level results and shifts into one visualization: spikes show victory margins and bend to show swing, styled like strands of hair.
items.title: Hairy election margins map

items.summary: A RAG question-answering system for real open-source issue trackers, evaluated on 95 hand-reviewed vitejs/vite questions with five configurations and scorer audits; retrieval improved weighted accuracy from 0.221 to 0.700 but raised fabrication from 1.1% to 20%.
items.title: zaxiu88888/issue-rag

items.summary: GPUWorks is a 40 MB GPU management and Model-as-a-Service platform that joins heterogeneous accelerators and public/private cloud instances into one cluster, deploying vLLM/SGLang models behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a 1,235-spec catalog.
items.title: Show HN: GPUWorks – A 40 MB GPU cluster manager for vLLM/SGLang, no K8s needed

items.summary: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is a generally available Gemini API/business video model adding native 15-second clips, multi-turn conversational editing, stronger reference adherence, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p.
items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

items.summary: Ork is a source-available assistant for persistent bots that share conversations and work on isolated computers, with Tauri desktop and Expo mobile apps backed by an API and worker; the repository provides local Docker/PostgreSQL setup steps.
items.title: orkbot-run/ork

items.summary: Winc is a Rust-built desktop editor with its own rendering engine, claiming 119 ms cold start, 52 MB RAM with 100,000 lines open, and a 1 GB file editable/highlighted in 220 ms; it includes multi-cursor editing, diffs, Git, terminal, previews and signed updates.
items.title: DEEIX-AI/Winc

items.summary: Rune is a pre-release native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and web with its own renderer, text, layout and springs; apps can run headless so agents can render PNGs, dump element trees and drive scripted input.
items.title: Rune: A native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and web

items.summary: Firenook is a Rust implementation of Firebase emulators, shown with a terminal UI and demo; its Show HN title claims 40× faster writes and 10× less RAM, and the text shows Firestore, Auth, Storage, Functions and Pub/Sub starting in about 600–800 ms.
items.title: Show HN: Firenook – Firebase emulators in Rust: 40× faster writes, 10× less RAM

items.summary: A blog post on emulating boolean values in CSS using the true/false keywords, @property to register a custom property constrained to syntax "true | false" with an initial value and inherits: false, plus @container style() queries for conditional styling.
items.title: true or false in CSS

items.summary: A Smashing Magazine article on making immersive LLM chat experiences (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and similar full-screen apps) accessible, framing accessibility as core to functional digital experiences and reframing chat UIs through WCAG and the social model of disability.
items.title: Making Immersive LLM Chat Experiences More Accessible
